question.text: A Category III AIF holds a portfolio of listed equities, unlisted equities, listed debt securities, and exchange-traded index futures. For which category of investment is an independent valuer MANDATORY under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Listed equities and exchange-traded index futures
Unlisted equities only — listed debt can use market prices
Unlisted securities AND listed debt securities
All four categories, regardless of market availability

explanation.text: The Logic: Category III AIFs shall undertake valuation of their investments in UNLISTED SECURITIES and LISTED DEBT SECURITIES by an independent valuer. Listed equities and exchange-traded derivatives are valued using market-determined prices (mark-to-market), so an independent valuer is not mandated for them. The Trap: Option B omits listed debt, which is explicitly covered by the independent-valuer requirement. Option A inverts the rule by including the very instruments that are marked to market. Option D over-extends the requirement to instruments that have observable market prices. Note: The mandate flows from the nature of the security — instruments without ready market quotes (unlisted, plus listed debt with thin trading) require independent valuation; deeply traded instruments do not.
